hypothesis: Turning an unsupported native-tool resolver dispatch into an explicit unresolved result will preserve the bounded merge safety gate while allowing builder runs to terminate in pending-merge recovery instead of dead-lettering.

metricsCompared.name: native-tool merge-conflict outcome
metricsCompared.baseline: merge-gate step threw before resolver dispatch and the workflow created an execution dead letter
metricsCompared.candidate: real Git/worktree conflict fixture returns pending-conflict after one non-dispatched resolver attempt and persists pending-merge metadata

metricsCompared.name: bounded resolver regression coverage
metricsCompared.baseline: KOTA-routable guard coverage passed while native tool control only asserted a thrown error
metricsCompared.candidate: 33 builder/git test files and 269 tests pass, including guarded KOTA routing and native Codex safe fallback

metricsCompared.name: merge safety posture
metricsCompared.baseline: native harness was prevented from bypassing KOTA tool guards by throwing
metricsCompared.candidate: native harness is still never invoked, conflicts remain unstaged and pending, and recovery review retains the preserved worktree

rationale: The change narrows failure handling without widening tool access: unsupported native-tool harnesses are not dispatched, the resolver records why it declined, and the existing merge gate owns the deterministic pending-merge state. Focused and full builder/git tests plus typecheck and lint prove the candidate behavior.
